sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:1
items.html: For this is a rule: coarseness and a screen cannot diminish or cause any flaw above the place where they are revealed, even in the slightest. And although the reflected light rises because of the screen in the vessel of Malchut and clothes all nine Sefirot from it upward, as above, nevertheless, the force of the coarseness in the screen does not rise upward at all. Therefore the nine Sefirot of Atzilut are regarded as being entirely without a screen. And although we discern many screens in the world of Atzilut as well, such as the screen of the Peh [mouth] and of the Chazeh [chest], etc., which applies in every particular Partzuf in Atzilut, the thing is that they are not actual screens; rather, they come from the inclusion of the lower one in the upper one. Only the screen of the Sium [end] of the legs of Atzilut is an actual screen, which stops the upper light, as written in Inner Observation here, in Chapter 14; study it there well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:2
items.html: That is, although the light that is in the world of Beria is necessarily drawn from the light of Ein Sof, for there is no illumination in the worlds that is not drawn from Ein Sof, nevertheless, since the light of Ein Sof that expands to Beria passes through a screen, its illumination is greatly diminished, until it is regarded that the light of Ein Sof has already stopped above the screen. And below, the ARI explains how light passes through a screen.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:3
items.html:
Explanation: It is a law in the upper worlds that any lower degree that causes an addition of light to the degree above it — that entire measure of added light is bestowed back upon the lower one that caused it. And so it is in our matter as well: the screen over Malchut of Atzilut caused the reflected light to rise, to clothe all nine Sefirot of Atzilut, and to become vessels for them, as above, such that without it the light of Ein Sof would not have been grasped and clothed in Atzilut, for no light is attained without a vessel, as is known. And since the screen caused that entire addition, namely the above-mentioned reflected light and ten Sefirot, therefore the screen and the vessel of Malchut widen because of the reflected light that returns and descends to it from the place of the screen downward, and it draws to itself all those ten Sefirot of Atzilut above, exactly in their likeness. Thus, Malchut of Atzilut alone goes, descends, and expands into ten Sefirot from her and within her, like the ten Sefirot of Atzilut, that is, from Keter to Malchut, and these are what are called the ten Sefirot of the world of Beria.
And this is what the ARI says: “Because of that striking of the upper light, which struck that curtain, and by force of those ten Sefirot of Atzilut that reached there, lights sparkled from them and passed through that screen, and became the ten Sefirot of Beria below.” That is, there are two things to understand here. The first discernment is the causing of the reflected light, which rises through the striking of the upper light on the screen; and it is the law of that reflected light to return and descend to the degree that caused its appearance, as above. The second discernment is the causing of the clothing of the self of the light of Ein Sof in the ten vessels of the reflected light that rose, which became the ten Sefirot of Atzilut above, as above; and it is their law too to return and descend below, to the degree that caused their appearance. Concerning the first discernment the ARI says, “because of the striking of the upper light on the curtain”: that is, this reflected light returns and descends from above downward to the world of Beria. And concerning the second discernment the ARI says, “and by force of those ten Sefirot of Atzilut,” etc. For from these two causes the ten Sefirot in the world of Beria were made.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:4
items.html: The appearance of reflected light is everywhere called by the name “sparkling.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:5
items.html: For all ten Sefirot of Atzilut were copied and stamped in the world of Beria, as written in the adjacent item. If so, the screen and Malchut were also stamped in the world of Beria, and that same coupling by striking of the upper light on the screen, and the ascents of reflected light, which rises and clothes all nine Sefirot of the world of Beria from the screen upward, apply there as well. This reflected light becomes ten vessels for the world of Beria, in which the self of the light of the world of Beria is clothed.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:6
items.html: Just as the reflected light of the screen of Atzilut returned and expanded from the screen downward and stamped the ten Sefirot of Beria, in the manner explained just above, item 3, see there, so in precisely the same manner the reflected light that rose from the screen of Malchut of Beria also returned and expanded downward, and stamped the ten Sefirot of the world of Yetzira. And likewise from Yetzira to Assiya.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:7
items.html:
As written further on, phase four, called Malchut, in which the screen was made, is herself divided into four phases of screen, by which all the kinds of changes and distinctions that appear in the worlds are brought about:
The screen of phase three serves in Atzilut, the screen of phase two serves in Beria, and the screen of phase one in Yetzira, as written below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:8
items.html: That is, the four phases of the coarsening, which are HB TM, which were called above the expansion of the light of Ein Sof to make vessels, and which are also called the ten Sefirot of direct light, for Tifferet includes six Sefirot, HGT NHY. And through the coupling by striking on the screen in the Sefira of Malchut of direct light, the light returns and rises in the secret of reflected light, and clothes all the above-mentioned particular ten Sefirot of direct light, and makes them all into one general degree, according to the measure of the level in the reflected light, as written below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:2:9
items.html: He is telling us by this that these four phases of direct light apply in every world and in every Partzuf, without any difference between a high degree and a low degree, and all the differences that are found in the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] and in the worlds are all only due to the screens and the reflected light in them, for the screen in one is not like the screen in another.
